growth_actions.instruction: Choose a reversible task with several visible flaws. Rank them by material risk, correct only the first, place the rest on tomorrow’s list, and stop at the criterion set in advance.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: Record whether deferred issues caused harm, how long delivery took, and whether physical tension eased after stopping. If material risk grew, revise the risk rule instead of forcing the exercise.
growth_actions.title: Correct one material issue and defer the rest

growth_actions.instruction: Before stating a standard, ask what risk the other person sees and summarize the answer in one sentence. Then separate required correction from personal preference.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: Note any information you had missed, whether the discussion reached a shared standard sooner, and whether you still expressed the boundary clearly.
growth_actions.title: Ask what risk the other person sees before stating the standard

growth_actions.instruction: Before a low-risk task, define minimum acceptance, one risk that must be controlled, and two details that may remain unfinished. Deliver when those conditions are met without raising the bar afterward.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: Compare the written standard with the outcome, any rework, and whether others could use the result. Mark which feared imperfections never became consequential.
growth_actions.title: Define “good enough” for one low-risk task

growth_actions.instruction: Leave one safe, repairable imperfection untouched for twenty-four hours. Record each urge to correct it and the reason without suppressing the discomfort.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: After twenty-four hours, check the actual consequence, attention consumed, and other people’s responses. If the issue mattered, document the evidence rather than calling the exercise a failure.
growth_actions.title: Observe one acceptable outcome after choosing not to correct immediately

growth_actions.instruction: Take one recent criticism and rewrite it as an observable fact, its impact, and a bounded request. Leave room for a response without adding a moral judgment.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: Keep the original and revised versions, then note whether the request could be answered, whether conflict intensity changed, and whether it addressed a material risk.
growth_actions.title: Turn one criticism into a specific request

sections.lead: If this candidate fits, attention may repeatedly return to standards, responsibility, and what could be improved.
paragraphs: When rules are vague or quality slips, you may first look for what would make the situation correct before addressing disappointment. That sequence across work, home, and private tasks is more informative than one instance of conscientiousness.

The protected need may be to act with integrity and remain accountable, rather than to be flawless. If standards relax easily in low-risk settings or tighten only under evaluation, role demands may explain the behavior better.
points: Repeatedly noticing deviation, ownership, and correctable gaps supports this candidate more than one isolated behavior.
If role accountability or a realistic need to prevent rework explains the pattern better, a stable type hypothesis deserves less weight.

sections.lead: You may notice standards, responsibility, and what could be improved earlier than people around you and allocate effort from there.
paragraphs: While others are still debating direction, you may already separate non-negotiable standards from details likely to create rework. The protected concern is often reliability and responsibility, not neatness alone.
In a low-risk task with no stated rules, voluntarily defining completion criteria supports this candidate. Doing so only under formal evaluation points more strongly to role demand.

sections.lead: The visible move may be to correct the deviation or clarify the rule before naming disappointment; the less spoken need may be to act with integrity without making flawlessness the price of self-respect.
paragraphs: Under pressure, you may check more often, correct details, tighten expectations, or become less flexible in order to restore order. That response can protect quality, but in a low-risk situation it can also narrow your options. This is an observable tendency, not a diagnosis or a confirmed defense mechanism.

Your effort to prevent errors may be heard as criticism or fault-finding. That possibility is a communication hypothesis: check what you intended, what the other person heard, and whether the risk was clear.
points: The visible move may be to check the rule and correct the problem; its purpose still requires contextual and first-person evidence.
Even when the aim is to act with integrity and dependable standards, another person’s reported impact remains independent evidence.

sections.lead: A possible habitual sequence is to spot a defect, contain irritation, tighten expectations, then scan for the next defect.
paragraphs: Possible pressure cues include missed responsibilities, confusing expectations, relaxed standards, overlooked problems, or effort that does not produce a dependable result. These are situations to observe; the report cannot determine what you fear or turn an inferred concern into psychological fact.

sections.lead: A mistyping risk is that professional rigor, role accountability, or a temporary high-stakes period can resemble this pattern.
paragraphs: You may label every correction as responsibility without separating material risk from preference or aesthetics. Ask what the correction actually protects, what evidence supports the risk, and what would happen if the detail remained imperfect.

If Type 1 doesn’t emerge as a major clue this time, think of it as a less prominent pattern: Watch to see if you’re less proactive in using standards, closures, and long-term responsibilities to calibrate your actions when rules are vague, quality drops, or responsibility boundaries are unclear. It's not a judgment that you lack a sense of principle.
points: Attention to deviation, ownership, and correctable gaps across work, relationships, and private choices carries more weight than behavior in one role.
Keep role accountability or a realistic need to prevent rework as a serious competing explanation.

sections.lead: You may show care through reliability, careful follow-through, and fixing what could cause harm.
paragraphs: Reliability, remembering details, and repairing problems may be ways you express care. In conflict, you may begin with facts, standards, and what needs to change. Add your feelings, the other person’s perspective, and the actual stakes so the discussion does not collapse into a verdict about who is right.
In a relationship with clear agreements and clear responsibilities, it may be easier for you to show that you care by being punctual, honoring your obligations, and handling problems cleanly.
points: Care may be expressed when you check the rule and correct the problem, but a type cannot specify what the other person needs.

sections.lead: A recurring relationship difficulty may be to revisit who was responsible and what would have been fair or appropriate.
paragraphs: You may be protecting quality or fairness, but if it's an issue right from the start, the other person may feel negated at first. First ask the other person if they are willing to listen to feedback, and then explain the impact of your concerns; repair in the relationship also requires the other person to be willing to respond, rather than just relying on you to make the standards clearer.

Repeated questions about rules, timing, or commitments may be an attempt to make the relationship dependable, but the immediate situation may also carry real risk. Ask which consequence matters most before interpreting the questions as criticism.

When requirements, acceptance criteria or delivery standards are still vague, it may be easier for you to break them into checklists, process nodes and review questions to help the team reduce rework.

sections.lead: In collaboration, you may value dependable handoffs and closed loops, with low tolerance for ambiguous ownership.
paragraphs: When you are quick to point out omissions, discrepancies, or inconsistencies, collaborators may first hear "being corrected" rather than hearing that you are protecting the quality of your delivery. A more negotiable approach is to first explain the risks, acceptance criteria, or common goals associated with this piece of feedback, and then distinguish between the parts that must be corrected and those that can be observed later; this is just a clue to communication friction, and it does not mean that you are necessarily picky or that others are necessarily resistant to feedback.
By explaining the risks, impacts, and shared goals before asking a question, you reduce the chance that others will interpret your warning as critical.
points: Collaboration can strain when concern with deviation, ownership, and correctable gaps is not translated into usable information and feedback.
Repair goals, ownership, and communication design before ruling out role accountability or a realistic need to prevent rework.

sections.lead: Around authority, you may over-check when leading and seek explicit standards and rationale when being led.
paragraphs: When you are in a leading, coordinating or reminding position, your influence may come from clarifying goals, standards, responsibilities and review mechanisms, so that delivery does not rely solely on personal awareness. It is suitable for use in scenarios where quality risks are high and processes are prone to drift; however, this only affects style cues and does not mean that the system determines that you have leadership capabilities or are suitable for management positions.

When others need to collaborate with you, assign tasks, or make requests, it may be easier to keep you engaged by clearly stating boundaries, priorities, acceptance criteria, and where trial and error are allowed. What is described here is a preference for collaboration. It is not a general prescription for management methods, nor does it necessarily mean that you need a high-control environment.
points: Clear authority makes it less necessary to act with integrity and dependable standards through guessing or repeated escalation.
Explicit decision rights and stopping conditions help prevent the pattern from starting to turn low-stakes preferences into principles.

sections.lead: You may remember details, initiate contact, offer practical help, and stay emotionally present.
paragraphs: Checking in, remembering details, and offering practical support may be ways you express care. Keep your capacity and your own needs visible so care remains a choice rather than an unspoken contract. In conflict, you may focus first on whether the bond has been damaged or whether your effort was seen. State the specific need or disappointment instead of waiting for the other person to infer it.

When the other person needs support or the interaction becomes cold, you may be more likely to take the initiative to approach, ask, and fill in; this shows a tendency to pay attention, but it does not mean that you must be responsible for maintaining the temperature of the relationship.

sections.lead: A recurring relationship difficulty may be to accumulate imbalance around giving, receiving, and whether effort was noticed.
paragraphs: You may express closeness with care, but unspoken needs are difficult to respond to accurately. Replace "I've done so much" in advance with "I need you to help me with something this time."

Offering help, checking on feelings, or remembering details may express care, although the person may simply hold responsibility in that moment. Name what you appreciated and ask what support is actually available instead of assuming an unlimited offer.

sections.lead: In collaboration, you may fill gaps and coordinate readily, sometimes accepting responsibilities that were never agreed.

sections.lead: Around authority, you may over-support when leading and need contribution to be seen without having boundaries ignored.

growth_actions.instruction: Reserve ten minutes each day for feelings that have not become useful output. Describe body cues, emotion, and need without converting them immediately into a plan or lesson.

growth_actions.title: Review body and relationship cost before starting the next target

growth_actions.instruction: Arrange time with someone that has no output, record, or display goal. Say explicitly that nothing needs to be achieved and keep the phone and task list out of view.

sections.lead: If this candidate fits, attention may repeatedly return to meaning, authenticity, what is missing, and the texture of personal experience.
paragraphs: You may first register whether an experience feels authentic, meaningful, and accurately yours, with particular sensitivity to what is absent or off-key. Emotional richness alone is insufficient; the question is whether difference repeatedly organizes choice.

Wanting accurate understanding is not the same as wanting to be special, and it may arise from a particular relationship or creative task. Stable engagement in ordinary, repetitive life is important counterevidence.

Nuance or emotional intensity may be heard as dissatisfaction, self-focus, or unwillingness to move on. Treat that as a possible communication gap and check what meaning you wanted to protect.

sections.lead: A mistyping risk is that creative training, grief, or a period of identity exploration can resemble this search for distinctiveness.
paragraphs: You may treat a strong feeling as proof that a situation has one meaning. Separate the feeling, the facts, and the story you are telling before deciding what action fits.

If Four doesn't emerge as a major clue this time, think of it as a less prominent pattern: Watch to see if you're less proactive in using authenticity, nuance, and unique perspective to calibrate your choices when you need to express differences, identify emotions, or illustrate personal meaning. It is not a judgment that you lack depth or have no self.

growth_actions.instruction: Each day, state your preference first in one small decision, including the option and timing, before hearing others. Do not withdraw it with “anything is fine.”

growth_actions.instruction: Place the most important task in the first available block and close one habitual activity before starting. Require only a minimum advance rather than the right overall mood.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: Compare progress, reduction in routine activity, and energy. Identify the trigger that most often removes the priority from view.
growth_actions.title: Put the most important task in the first work block

growth_actions.instruction: For one delayed decision, set a date, required information, and a default option at expiry. Once information is sufficient, do not use further coordination to postpone choice.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: Record whether the deadline held, the cost of delay, and unresolved disagreement. Allow only one replacement date with a written reason.
growth_actions.title: Set a firm deadline for one delayed decision

growth_actions.instruction: Before agreeing, repeat what you will own, what you will not own, and what the other person must carry. Wait for confirmation before beginning.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: Check whether the commitment stayed clear, whether resentment or forgetting decreased, and whether you expanded scope merely to restore harmony.
growth_actions.title: Restate what you genuinely agree to before saying yes

growth_actions.instruction: Track the twenty-four hours after voicing one disagreement: the response, relationship change, and issue progress. Do not use immediate tension to predict permanent rupture.
growth_actions.observable_outcome: Compare expected and actual consequences, keeping evidence of continued stability alongside facts that require repair or a renewed boundary.

sections.reflection_question: Review one conflict intensified by the tension between useful coordination from lowering your own priority. What was the first observable signal, and where could repair begin with facts, feelings, and a bounded request?
sections.title: How conflict escalates and how repair can begin

sections.lead: In task settings, you may tend to understand system-wide impact and pacing, contributing strongly to integration and continuity.
paragraphs: At work, your attention may go first to alignment, sustainable pace, suppressed disagreement, and whether cooperation can continue. This does not establish job fit, competence, or performance.
When multiple parties have split opinions, inconsistent rhythms, or tense relationships, it may be easier for you to keep everyone discussing at the same table.
points: The tendency to absorb disagreement, lower tension, and postpone a position can support quality or pace at the right task stage.
As the stage changes, reassess whether investment in overall stability, other viewpoints, friction cost, and familiar pace still fits.
sections.reflection_question: During a task stage when people move at conflicting speeds, friction appears, or your position may disturb the balance, how did this way of working improve quality or pace? At what later stage did it need to be complemented by a different strategy?
sections.title: How tasks move and the conditions that help

sections.lead: In collaboration, you may build consensus but need explicit personal judgment, deadlines, and non-negotiables.
paragraphs: If you wait for the situation to naturally stabilize, you may miss a critical window and the team may not know your true position. You can set a time point in advance when you must express your stance, and give a low-intensity version first: what do I prefer, what other concerns do I have, and who needs additional information.
You don’t need to explain everything at once, just express the most certain point at the moment.
points: Collaboration can strain when concern with overall stability, other viewpoints, friction cost, and familiar pace is not translated into usable information and feedback.
Repair goals, ownership, and communication design before ruling out a coordination role or a situation that truly needs de-escalation.
sections.reflection_question: In a recent collaboration friction involving useful coordination from lowering your own priority, was the missing ingredient information, feedback design, ownership, or psychological safety? What evidence shows that type need not explain it?
sections.title: Information, feedback, and friction in collaboration

sections.lead: Around authority, you may coordinate inclusively when leading and need gentle but definite priorities and follow-through when led.
paragraphs: When you're in a position of alignment, influence can come from muting the noise, embracing dissent, and allowing the rhythm to be uninterrupted by mood swings. It prompts integrated influence clues, which does not mean that you are naturally suitable for leadership, nor does it mean that team differences can only be resolved through gentleness in the long term.

When someone needs your opinion, giving the question, context, and alternative expressions in advance may make it easier for your true thoughts to emerge. It indicates a low-pressure expression of preference and does not mean that you lack a stance or can only passively cooperate.
points: Clear authority makes it less necessary to stay connected while making personal priority visible through guessing or repeated escalation.
Explicit decision rights and stopping conditions help prevent the pattern from starting to trade personal priority for immediate ease.
sections.reflection_question: In delegating, leading, or being managed when people move at conflicting speeds, friction appears, or your position may disturb the balance, which authority or stopping condition remained unclear? What observable outcome would change if it were explicit?
sections.title: Leading and being led: authority, boundaries, and interaction

sections.lead: As pressure rises, you may shift into secondary tasks, slow action, and appear agreeable while resisting internally.
paragraphs: The more an issue requires a position or a difficult choice, the easier it becomes to postpone.
Organizing, scrolling, or low-effort work takes over while the important decision remains untouched.
points: Pressure may amplify the impulse to absorb disagreement, lower tension, and postpone a position until it begins to trade personal priority for immediate ease.
Sleep, workload, and a coordination role or a situation that truly needs de-escalation must be checked alongside a type hypothesis.
sections.reflection_question: As pressure rose when people move at conflicting speeds, friction appears, or your position may disturb the balance, which action intensified first? What did it protect, when did it narrow choice, and could sleep, workload, or real risk explain it better?
sections.title: How the habit intensifies or changes under pressure

sections.lead: With more safety, you may recognize preferences sooner, decide proactively, and tolerate short-term disagreement.
paragraphs: You may bring patience and continuity to work that depends on steady maintenance rather than short bursts of novelty.
You may understand competing positions without requiring yourself to surrender your own.
points: When safety increases, the impulse to absorb disagreement, lower tension, and postpone a position is no longer the only familiar response.
Look for flexibility while attending to overall stability, other viewpoints, friction cost, and familiar pace, not evidence that you have become another type.
sections.reflection_question: When you felt safe and unhurried, did a different response appear—for example, the relationship holds after you state a disagreement? How could you tell that safety, rather than a different task, accounted for the change?
sections.title: What becomes possible when safety increases

sections.lead: Growth can mean learning to occupy space promptly while preserving connection through small, explicit choices.
paragraphs: In one small decision this week, state your preference, your reason, and what remains negotiable. If you need time, say exactly when you will return to the discussion.
Start with a low-stakes choice and practice making your position visible.
points: Growth adds an optional step before you absorb disagreement, lower tension, and postpone a position; it does not require erasing the original tendency.
Use seven days of evidence to test whether the new choice can stay connected while making personal priority visible without the familiar cost.
sections.reflection_question: The next time when people move at conflicting speeds, friction appears, or your position may disturb the balance, what small choice could you add without discarding your existing strength? What behavioral evidence after seven days would count as useful?
sections.title: Growth means adding choice, not becoming another type

sections.lead: The nine levels are a theoretical reading framework. For Type 9, The Peacemaker, they can organize observations about how overall stability, shared pace, friction, and every party’s place changes with resources and pressure, but this score cannot locate you at a level.

sections.lead: Early signals may include saying “anything is fine,” choosing low-priority tasks, or repeatedly delaying a decision.
paragraphs: Start with one low-conflict statement: name your current preference or minimum position without trying to resolve the whole disagreement.
Begin with ‘I currently prefer…’ without requiring yourself to make a final decision.
points: When you first begin to trade personal priority for immediate ease, bodily, behavioral, and relational signals often arrive before the later explanation.
Recovery restores choice while checking whether a coordination role or a situation that truly needs de-escalation still requires practical or professional support.
sections.reflection_question: For moments when people move at conflicting speeds, friction appears, or your position may disturb the balance, name one bodily, one behavioral, and one relational early signal. Which low-cost recovery step comes first, and when would another form of support be appropriate?
sections.title: Early signals and routes back to choice

entries.short_title: Reduces friction through steadiness and coordination

core_motivation_difference.1: When a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression, Type 1, The Reformer is more likely to organize action around standards, responsibility, and correctable gaps in order to act with integrity without making flawlessness the price of self-respect. This side gains support when the first adjustment concerns standards, boundaries, or ownership.
core_motivation_difference.4: Facing the same case where a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression, Type 4, The Individualist is more likely to organize action around meaning, authenticity, absence, and the texture of experience in order to be accurately understood while staying connected through ordinary life. This side is more informative when the first adjustment concerns the resources or relationships attached to that focus.

fear_difference.1: When a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression, concern for Type 1, The Reformer tends to rise as standards, responsibility, and correctable gaps becomes less controllable. A counterexample is sustained concern about meaning, authenticity, absence, and the texture of experience even after the first condition improves.
fear_difference.4: Under the same conditions, Type 4, The Individualist is more likely to become uneasy when meaning, authenticity, absence, and the texture of experience is threatened. If restoring that condition leaves attention fixed on standards, responsibility, and correctable gaps, keep the other candidate open.

relationship_difference.1: In a relationship where a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression, Type 1, The Reformer may show care through reliability, reminders, and repair. When the response disappoints, the first concern often still involves standards, responsibility, and correctable gaps.
relationship_difference.4: In that same situation, Type 4, The Individualist may instead show care through depth, tailored expression, and emotional detail. Compared with Type 1, The Reformer, check whether a missing response first registers as neglect of meaning, authenticity, absence, and the texture of experience.

entries.resonance_feedback_prompt: Mark only observations supported by an event record or another person’s feedback. Familiarity, preference, and a single behavior cannot decide between Type 1, The Reformer and Type 4, The Individualist.
entries.seven_day_observation_question: For seven days, record three events resembling “a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression.” Did the first cue, first action, and later cost fit standards, responsibility, and correctable gaps or meaning, authenticity, absence, and the texture of experience more closely? Keep one event that neither candidate explains well.
entries.shared_surface_similarity: When a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression, Type 1, The Reformer and Type 4, The Individualist may both look invested, alert, or willing to take responsibility. The useful distinction is whether attention first moves toward standards, responsibility, and correctable gaps or meaning, authenticity, absence, and the texture of experience.
entries.short_compare_copy: Type 1, The Reformer first tracks standards, responsibility, and correctable gaps; Type 4, The Individualist first tracks meaning, authenticity, absence, and the texture of experience. Compare the sequence in one real setting without forcing a choice.

stress_reaction_difference.1: As pressure rises while a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression, Type 1, The Reformer may tighten standards and magnify defects. Notice whether this begins before the information is complete and what it protects in the short term.
stress_reaction_difference.4: Under pressure from a situation where a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression, Type 4, The Individualist is more likely to magnify absence and comparison until mood steers action. The question is whether that sequence repeats here and elsewhere, not which response is better.

work_difference.1: At work, Type 1, The Reformer is likely to clarify standards, material risk, and completion criteria first when a piece of work needs accuracy without losing personal expression. This is a sequence of attention, not a rating of competence, performance, or job fit.

fallback_template.motivation_difference: Please go back to the core motivation: What do you care more about: standards, relationship position, safety, boundaries, freedom, results, authenticity, or a sense of stability?
fallback_template.observation_question: In the next 7 days, only specific situations, trigger points, first reactions and post-event reviews will be recorded: In key scenes, do you give priority to standards, relationship position, safety, boundaries, freedom, results, sense of reality, or overall stability? Also note counterexamples: scenarios that look like candidates for a certain type, but what really drives you is not its core focus. Close-call is a side-by-side analysis portal. It is not a forced choice, nor can it lead to diagnosis, recruitment screening, ability evaluation or career decision.
fallback_template.pressure_difference: Under pressure, do you more often correct, confirm, disengage, please, toughen, deflect, or calm the situation first?
fallback_template.relationship_difference: In a relationship, how would you rather be treated: to be understood, recognized, needed, to have boundaries respected, to be committed, or to put an end to conflict first?
fallback_template.same_surface: Both may explain some of the similarities in surface style, but the disagreement is usually not about appearance, but about which type of attention is activated first in stressful situations.
fallback_template.work_difference: When advancing tasks, what do you give more priority to: quality, results, risk, space, dominance, or overall stability?

result_overview.clear.body_template: This answer presents a relatively concentrated primary candidate, which can be used to sort out recent common motivations, attention and coping methods. Please treat this result as an observable, retrospective explanatory hypothesis rather than an absolute label or diagnostic conclusion on personality.
result_overview.clear.title_template: The current primary candidates are relatively clear

result_overview.close_call.body_template: The first two candidates are close in this response. Compare their stress triggers, relationship expectations, work patterns, and conflict reactions side by side, and look for recent situations that contradict either candidate. For the next seven days, record the situation, trigger, first reaction, and later reflection without fixing a personality label.
result_overview.close_call.title_template: The leading candidates need close-call comparison

result_overview.diffuse.body_template: Signals are spread across several types, so the first candidate does not support a single-type conclusion. result_overview.low_quality.body_template: The results are still readable this time, but the response signal shows that the boundaries of interpretation need to be relaxed: it is more suitable for helping you look back at which questions, situations, or states affected your choices, and is not suitable for confirming the primary type, evaluating personality stability, or inferring ability. This prompt does not blame the respondent, nor does it mean that you are not serious; it only shows that the answer sheet does not provide an interpretable signal to the system. A more prudent next step is to retest the same question type when your attention and state are more stable; switching to another form can only be used as a supplementary observation and cannot be regarded as finding better answers or comparing across question types.
result_overview.low_quality.title_template: The current result has a quality boundary

entries.copy: The E105 five-point Likert form uses rating responses to form a full nine-type profile, top three candidates, a leading-candidate gap, and close-call comparison within one scoring context. It is a starting point for self-observation, and its scores are interpreted only within E105.

The FC144 two-option forced-choice form records relative preference signals across paired choices and can provide another observation after a close-call result. Both forms have the same evidence status. FC144 does not replace E105's primary candidate, top three candidates, or raw scoring facts, and its results are interpreted only within the FC144 scoring context.

E105 and FC144 use the same Enneagram interpretation framework but different response tasks, scoring sources, and error structures, so they do not share a scoring space. History, sharing, PDF, and retest surfaces retain each form's source. The page does not directly compare their values or interpret cross-form differences in the top three candidates as personality change.

Cross-form comparison is disabled. Unless a validated equivalence mapping becomes available, E105 and FC144 remain in separate scoring contexts, and history, sharing, and result-review surfaces do not infer improvement, decline, health status, or measurement precision from their differences.

This result supports personality-pattern reflection, self-observation, and dialogue. Current research does not support treating the Enneagram as a well-validated clinical scale. It is not used for mental-health judgment, treatment recommendations, hiring, job matching, competency evaluation, or individual risk assessment. Scores, leading candidates, close-call, diffuse, and response-quality states remain hypotheses to check against real situations.

A user-confirmed type records the user's own resonance after observation. It is not a system rescore or external confirmation. History and sharing surfaces present it only as a self-observation note; it does not overwrite the primary candidate, top three candidates, scorer output, or original scoring facts.

When triggered by low-quality signals, the results are still readable, but the interpretation boundaries are significantly narrowed. The page only retains light observation suggestions to avoid extending a single low-stability answer into a deterministic type of judgment; it gives priority to suggestions for retesting the same question type when the state is more stable and time is more sufficient. Switching forms can serve as another observation, but should not be used as a way to circumvent quality boundaries, find better answers, demonstrate personality changes, or compare score gains and losses.

Diffuse means the nine type signals do not yet form a clear leading pattern. The page lowers certainty about any one number and prioritizes the top three candidates, center distribution, recent counterexamples, and a seven-day observation task. Retesting provides another response sample; it does not automatically correct the result to a particular type.

A close-call means the first and second candidates are close. The page turns their differences into side-by-side comparison, counterexample checks, and seven-day observation questions without requiring a forced type decision.

growth_actions.instruction: 选一项已经看见多个瑕疵、但后果可逆的任务。先按实际风险排序，只修排在第一的问题，其余写入次日清单；达到预设停止点后不再追加检查。
growth_actions.observable_outcome: 记录被暂缓的问题是否真的造成损失、交付用了多少时间，以及停止后身体紧绷是否下降；若关键风险扩大，应调整风险分级而不是坚持练习。
growth_actions.title: 只修一个关键问题，其余记入明日清单

growth_actions.instruction: 下一次准备指出标准前，先问对方最担心的风险，并用一句话复述答案。随后说明你的判断，明确哪些是必须修正、哪些只是偏好。
growth_actions.observable_outcome: 核对对方是否补充了你原先没有的信息、讨论是否更快进入共同标准，以及你是否仍能清楚表达底线。
growth_actions.title: 提出标准前先询问对方看到的风险

growth_actions.instruction: 开始一个低风险任务前，写下最低可接受标准、必须守住的一项风险和可以留白的两处细节。达到标准即交付，不在完成后改写门槛。
growth_actions.observable_outcome: 比较预设标准与最终结果，记录是否发生返工、他人是否能正常使用，以及哪些“必须更好”的预期没有成为事实。
growth_actions.title: 为低风险任务预先定义“足够好”

growth_actions.instruction: 刻意保留一处容易修正且不影响安全的小偏差，至少二十四小时不处理。期间只记录想纠正的次数和触发理由，不用压抑不适。
growth_actions.observable_outcome: 二十四小时后检查实际后果、注意力消耗和他人反应；如果偏差确实重要，记录判断依据，而不是把练习解释成失败。
growth_actions.title: 记录一次没有立刻纠错但结果仍可接受的经历

growth_actions.instruction: 选一句最近浮现的批评，把它拆成可观察事实、实际影响和一个有限请求。提出请求后给对方回应空间，不追加道德评价。
growth_actions.observable_outcome: 保存原句与改写句，记录对方能否明确回应、冲突强度是否改变，以及请求是否真正对应关键风险。
growth_actions.title: 把一条批评改写成具体请求

sections.lead: 如果这个候选贴近你，注意力可能反复落在标准、责任与可改进之处。
paragraphs: 当规则含糊或质量出现偏差时，你可能先寻找“怎样才算做对”，随后才处理自己的不满。这个顺序若在工作、家庭和独处任务里反复出现，才比一次认真负责更有辨识力。
需要守住的也许不是完美本身，而是做事正当、可靠、能够承担后果。若你在低风险场景很容易放下标准，或主要在被考核时才变得严谨，角色要求可能是更好的解释。
points: 反复先看到偏差、责任与可改进之处，比单次行为更能支持这个候选。
若主要由职责要求或对返工的现实预防解释，就不必把表现归为稳定模式。
sections.reflection_question: 回看一次发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时的经历：你的注意力最先去了哪里？哪项事实支持这个候选，哪项事实更接近“低风险处能够自然停手”这个反例？
sections.title: 这种模式的整体画像

sections.lead: 你可能比周围人更早留意标准、责任与可改进之处，并据此分配精力。
paragraphs: 你可能在别人还讨论方向时，已经开始分辨哪些是底线、哪些会留下返工。标准感真正保护的常是可靠与责任，而不只是整齐或个人偏好。
观察低风险任务：若没有明确规范时你仍会主动建立完成条件，1号线索会更有分量；若只在考核场景如此，职责解释更充分。
points: 注意力落点常透露正在保护的东西：让行动正当可靠。
用真实取舍核对动机，并排除职责要求或对返工的现实预防的影响。
sections.reflection_question: 在发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时，你最想守住的究竟是什么？怎样用实际后果区分关键风险与个人偏好？
sections.title: 你会优先注意什么、想守住什么

sections.lead: 外在常见的是：先指出偏差、补齐规则，再表达担心或失望；较难直接说出的需要可能是确认自己做得正当、可靠并经得起检验。
paragraphs: 压力上来时，你可能更容易借助检查、纠偏、收口、自我要求或把边界讲清楚来恢复可控感。
一种常见误读假设是：你的提醒被听成挑剔，而不是被理解为在降低返工、风险或不公平。它只提示可能的沟通落差，不能替别人判断他们怎样看你，也不能证明你的动机一定如此。
points: 外在动作可能是检查标准并纠正问题，内在用意仍需由本人和情境共同核对。
当目标是让行动正当可靠时，别人报告的实际影响仍是独立证据。
sections.reflection_question: 选一次发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时、别人只看到你的做法却未必理解用意的互动：你做了什么、希望保护什么，对方的反馈又提供了什么不同解释？
sections.title: 外在表现与不易说出口的需要

sections.lead: 这类惯性循环可能是：察觉不妥后压住恼怒，继而提高要求、反复纠错。
paragraphs: 这一型相关的压力线索通常出现在失责、混乱、标准被放松、重要问题被带过，或努力没有形成清楚结果时。
压力信号可从反复检查、对小偏差反应变快、满意感下降、身体紧绷等可观察行为检查起。
points: 围绕偏差、责任与可改进之处的惯性，会沿注意、解释、情绪与动作逐步收窄。
找到检查标准并纠正问题之前的停顿点，才能看见仍可选择的回应。
sections.reflection_question: 最近一次发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时，情绪、解释和动作按什么顺序发生？如果在第二步暂停，哪一种不同回应仍然可行？
sections.title: 情绪怎样推动惯性循环

sections.lead: 容易误认之处是：把角色责任、专业训练或短期高压造成的严谨都解释成稳定类型。
paragraphs: 你可能把每一次纠偏都理解成“负责”，却没有区分关键风险、审美偏好和低影响细节。复盘时可以问：这次坚持实际保护了什么，是否有证据显示后果严重，还是主要缓解了自己的不安。
如果 1 号这次没有成为主要线索，可把它当作一个低动用资源假设：观察自己在规则模糊、质量下降或责任边界不清时，是否较少主动使用标准、收口和长期责任来校准行动。
points: 对偏差、责任与可改进之处的关注跨工作、关系和独处反复出现，才比单一角色表现更有辨识力。
职责要求或对返工的现实预防是需要认真保留的替代解释。
sections.reflection_question: 围绕关键风险与个人偏好，哪些跨情境证据支持这个候选？哪些相同行为更可能来自职责、文化、短期压力或习得习惯？
sections.title: 怎样辨认，也怎样避免误认

sections.lead: 1号完美型与9号和平型、2号助人型相邻；邻位理论用于比较长期表达，不能由第二高分或一次行为直接判定翼型。
paragraphs: 阅读邻位时，可比较标准、责任与可改进之处与相邻类型各自优先保护的对象，而不要把分数排序写成身份结论。
箭头、翼型、亚型与发展层次都属于理论阅读层；当前结果只呈现同一题型内的相对分布。
points: 相邻类型：9、2
第二高分不等于翼型
用长期情境和反例观察，不自动分配箭头、亚型或层次
sections.reflection_question: 如果相邻类型的描述也有共鸣，哪一种核心关注更能解释你在发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时时的取舍？哪些证据仍不足以判断邻位倾向？
sections.title: 邻位倾向应该怎样理解

sections.lead: 当你有余地时，这一模式可能帮助你把模糊要求整理成可执行标准，在风险出现前补上漏洞。
paragraphs: 线索较有余地时，标准感可能表现为清晰、公正、可靠和愿意改善系统。
在标准会影响质量或边界的场景里，如果你能说明背后的目的，别人更容易把你的坚持理解成保护结果，而不是单纯挑错。
points: 有余地时，关注偏差、责任与可改进之处可以转化为具体贡献。
资源性表达既能让行动正当可靠，也会为其他做法保留空间。
sections.reflection_question: 在你有余地且发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时的一次事件里，这种注意方式具体帮助了谁、解决了什么问题？什么条件使它成为资源而不是自动反应？
sections.title: 有余地时，这种模式怎样发挥作用

sections.lead: 同一倾向失去弹性时，可能开始把偏好升级为原则，让自己和别人长期处在被审查的位置。
paragraphs: 负荷较高时，纠偏和自我要求可能变多。
在已经足够的场景里，你可能仍想继续加码，仿佛放松会带来失守；这可以作为区分关键风险和低风险事项的提醒。
points: 短期有效不等于长期无代价；关键拐点是把低风险偏好也升级成原则。
用后续影响区分这种代价与职责要求或对返工的现实预防，不用类型名称替行为辩护。
sections.reflection_question: 同一种做法最近何时越过了收益拐点？请分别记录短期好处、后续代价，以及“低风险处能够自然停手”是否可能是更合适的选择。
sections.title: 同一种倾向，何时从资源变成代价

sections.lead: 你的用意可能是好的，但本意是保护质量，实际可能让他人只听见批评和不信任。
paragraphs: 常见张力是：一方面重视把事情做稳、做清楚，另一方面也需要判断哪些场景允许不完整、试错或暂时放下。
关系或合作中，如果别人最先听到的是不足，可能较难感到你的善意；表达顺序会影响反馈被接收的方式。
points: 想要让行动正当可靠，不保证检查标准并纠正问题会被别人按同样方式理解。
围绕偏差、责任与可改进之处，把用意、行为和实际影响分开复盘才有修复入口。
sections.reflection_question: 挑一次发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时且用意与影响不一致的互动：你原本想守住什么，对方实际接收到什么，哪句澄清最可能缩小这段落差？
sections.title: 你的用意与实际影响可能怎样错位

sections.lead: 你可能通过用守约、提醒、修正细节和承担后果表达在乎。
paragraphs: 关系里，你可能通过可靠、兑现和修问题表达在乎；这需要结合真实互动理解，不能只用类型推断关系需求。
在约定清楚、责任明确的关系里，你可能更容易用守时、兑现和把问题处理干净来表达在乎。
points: 在乎可能体现为检查标准并纠正问题，但对方需要什么不能由类型代答。
直接询问支持是否被接住，也能检验让行动正当可靠是否真是当时重点。
sections.reflection_question: 在容易涉及关键风险与个人偏好的关系里，你最近怎样表达在乎？直接询问对方把它体验为支持、压力还是别的东西；答案与预期有何不同？
sections.title: 怎样表达在乎，又期待怎样被对待

sections.lead: 关系里容易反复出现的是：容易在谁更负责、什么才算合理上反复拉扯。
paragraphs: 你可能是在保护质量或公平，但如果一开口就是问题，对方可能先感到被否定。先问对方是否愿意听反馈，再说明你担心的影响；关系里的修复也需要对方愿意回应，而不是只靠你把标准说得更清楚。
当他反复确认规则、时间或承诺时，可能是在把关系放进可依赖的结构；也可能只是当前事项风险高。先问他最担心哪一步，而不是直接理解为挑剔。
points: 关系难题容易在把低风险偏好也升级成原则时重复，而不只发生在某一位对象身上。
边界、权力与沟通历史可能比偏差、责任与可改进之处更能解释一次具体冲突。
sections.reflection_question: 哪一种关系难题在不同对象之间重复出现？其中哪些环节与关键风险与个人偏好有关，哪些其实由边界、权力或沟通习惯造成？
sections.title: 容易反复出现的关系难题

sections.lead: 冲突可能这样升级：从事实和原则进入冲突，越着急越像在宣判对错。
paragraphs: 冲突中，你可能先抓事实、标准和应当如何处理。建议把它当作沟通观察点，同时补充感受、需要和对方视角，避免把冲突归因于固定人格。
我刚才像是在挑错，其实我担心的是这件事会影响后面哪一步；我先把影响说清楚。
points: 冲突升级时，偏差、责任与可改进之处可能压过对感受和共同目标的说明。
修复要让让行动正当可靠变成对方可以回应的具体请求，而非人格判断。
sections.reflection_question: 复盘一次因关键风险与个人偏好而升级的冲突：第一个可观察信号是什么？如果先说事实、感受和具体请求，修复会从哪里开始？
sections.title: 冲突如何升级，又怎样修复

sections.lead: 在任务中，你可能倾向于先厘清规范、风险和完成标准，再稳定推进。
paragraphs: 在工作里，你可能更容易先检查标准是否清楚、流程是否可执行、责任边界是否被尊重，以及交付是否达到可接受质量。它可能帮助你解释为什么会重视校准和纠偏，但不能替代能力、经验、兴趣、组织环境和绩效证据来判断岗位适配。
当需求、验收口径或交付标准还含糊时，你可能较容易把它们拆成检查清单、流程节点和复盘问题，帮助团队减少返工。
points: 检查标准并纠正问题在合适任务阶段可以形成效率或质量优势。
任务阶段变化后，要重新判断对偏差、责任与可改进之处的投入是否仍然匹配。
sections.reflection_question: 在发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时的任务阶段，这种推进方式怎样提高了质量或速度？换到什么阶段后，它反而需要另一种工作策略补足？
sections.title: 推进任务的方式与发挥条件

sections.lead: 协作中，你可能表现为：重视承诺兑现与问题闭环，对含糊交付较敏感。
paragraphs: 当你很快指出遗漏、偏差或不一致时，协作者可能先听到“被纠正”，而不是听到你在保护交付质量。更可协商的做法是先说明这条反馈关联的风险、验收口径或共同目标，再区分必须修正和可以后续观察的部分。
提出问题前先说明风险、影响和共同目标，能降低别人把提醒听成挑剔的概率。
points: 协作摩擦可能来自偏差、责任与可改进之处没有被翻译成清楚的信息和反馈。
先修正目标、责任与沟通设计，再排除职责要求或对返工的现实预防这类情境因素。
sections.reflection_question: 最近一次涉及关键风险与个人偏好的协作摩擦中，缺的是信息、反馈方式、责任边界还是心理安全？哪项证据说明问题不必归因于类型？
sections.title: 协作中的信息、反馈与摩擦

sections.lead: 在权责情境中，带人时容易亲自把关；被管理时需要清楚的标准和决策依据。
paragraphs: 当你处在牵头、协调或提醒位置时，影响力可能来自把目标、标准、责任和复盘机制讲清楚，让交付不只依赖个人自觉。它适合用于质量风险高、流程容易漂移的场景。
当别人需要与你协作、分配任务或提出要求时，清楚说明边界、优先级、验收标准和哪些地方允许试错，可能更容易让你稳定投入。
points: 授权清楚时，让行动正当可靠不必靠猜测或持续加码来维持。
明确权限与停止条件，可以防止把低风险偏好也升级成原则成为默认管理方式。
sections.reflection_question: 在容易出现发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时的授权、带人或接受管理场景里，哪项权限与停止条件没有说清？把它明确后，什么结果会改变？
sections.title: 带人与被管理：授权、边界和互动

sections.lead: 压力升高时，你可能会收紧控制、放大瑕疵，对自己和他人的容错都下降。
paragraphs: 原本可以先讨论的问题，被你迅速拉到需要马上修正。
完成后主要看见缺口，很少停下来确认哪些部分已经达到要求。
points: 压力可能放大检查标准并纠正问题，直到它开始把低风险偏好也升级成原则。
睡眠、工作量和职责要求或对返工的现实预防必须与类型假设一起检查。
sections.reflection_question: 当发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时且压力升高时，你最先增加的动作是什么？它短期保护了什么，何时开始压缩选择，又可能被哪些现实因素更好地解释？
sections.title: 压力下，惯性怎样加重或变形

sections.lead: 安全感增加时，你可能更能承认多种做法都可行，也更愿意让轻松和乐趣进入过程。
paragraphs: 在你有授权和资源时，你可能不只指出问题，也愿意把改善落到流程、文档或机制更新上。
当任务涉及安全、承诺或长期信任时，你不轻易把底线让给短期效率，这类谨慎可能有价值；低风险场景仍需要区分必要标准和过度加码。
points: 安全感增加时，检查标准并纠正问题不再是唯一熟悉的回应。
观察能否在关注偏差、责任与可改进之处时仍保留弹性，而非寻找另一种人格。
sections.reflection_question: 在足够安全且不赶时间时，是否出现“低风险处能够自然停手”这样的不同表达？怎样确认变化来自安全感，而非任务性质不同？
sections.title: 感到安全时，哪些表达会出现

sections.lead: 成长可以理解为：在重要原则与个人偏好之间分级，把“足够好”也纳入负责。
paragraphs: 成长轴先从一次低风险校准开始：保留关键标准，同时选一处允许“足够好”的范围，观察结果是否真的变差。
把其余问题记录下来但不立刻处理，观察是否真的失控。
points: 成长目标是为检查标准并纠正问题增加一个可选步骤，不是消除原有倾向。
用七天证据判断新选择能否兼顾让行动正当可靠与现实影响。
sections.reflection_question: 面对发现标准被放松、责任含糊或成果仍有瑕疵时，下一次你愿意增加哪个小选择，同时保留原有优势？七天后用什么行为证据判断它是否有效？
sections.title: 成长方向：增加选择，而不是换一种人格

sections.lead: 九个发展层次是九型理论中的阅读框架；对于1号完美型，可用它观察“标准、责任与可改进之处”的表达怎样随资源和压力改变，但不能据本次分数判断你位于哪一层。

levels.description: 线索较有余地时，标准、责任与秩序可能成为清晰行动的资源。
levels.observation_prompt: 在标准会影响质量或边界的场景里，如果你能说明背后的目的，别人更容易把你的坚持理解成保护结果，而不是单纯挑错。
levels.title: 理论层次 1

levels.title: 理论层次 2

levels.observation_prompt: 线索较有余地时，标准感可能表现为清晰、公正、可靠和愿意改善系统。
levels.title: 理论层次 3

levels.description: 多数普通情境里，你可能会扫描偏差、责任和完成度；具体强度需要结合任务风险观察。
levels.observation_prompt: 多数普通情境里，你可能会自然扫描偏差、责任和完成度，并希望事情更有章法。
levels.title: 理论层次 4

levels.description: 常见张力是：一方面重视把事情做稳、做清楚，另一方面也需要判断哪些场景允许不完整、试错或暂时放下。

levels.title: 理论层次 5

levels.description: 在已经足够的场景里，你可能仍想继续加码，仿佛放松会带来失守；这可以作为区分关键风险和低风险事项的提醒。
levels.observation_prompt: 压力下，你可能更快进入对错和标准语言，而较晚承认自己已经累了；这提示复盘时也要看资源消耗。
levels.title: 理论层次 6

levels.description: 负荷叠加时，纠偏和自我要求可能变多。
levels.observation_prompt: 负荷较高时，纠偏和自我要求可能变多。
levels.title: 理论层次 7

levels.description: 如果每件事都按无遗憾标准处理，恢复和试错空间可能被压缩；可先识别哪些事项真的需要高标准。
levels.observation_prompt: 同一件事反复检查很多遍，仍很难停在已经足够的版本。
levels.title: 理论层次 8

levels.description: 原本可以先讨论的问题，被你迅速拉到需要马上修正。
